tools.title: Abandon stale rollout
tools.description: Releases the execution claim of one stale rollout job of an owned stack so that the stack can be retried with `retry-rollout`. Only a job that stopped reporting can be abandoned; any other job answers 409 `abandon_job_conflict` with the guard that refused. The body is empty and no command is sent to a server.

tools.title: Abort workload relocation
tools.description: Stops a relocation that has not finished and resumes the workloads on the source server, whose data was kept. The body must carry `owner_approved: true`. A relocation that already moved cannot be aborted (409), and an abort stays fenced until the nodes verify the state.

tools.title: Add one managed Node through native provider control
tools.description: Creates or resumes one deterministic Add-Server job for the exact owned StackKit deployment. The standard `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory. Replaying the same key with the same canonical request returns the original job, lease, runtime-server, resource-generation, and provider-operation correlations; reusing it with different intent fails with 409. The raw key is never persisted or returned. A lost response or an uncertain native-admission outcome remains resumable only with the same key. HTTP acceptance means native admission is durable and provider reconciliation is pending; it never claims that the VM is already provisioned or healthy. Fresh admission atomically reserves the authenticated tenant/owner capacity slot with the lease generation and provider operation. When authoritative native admission finds that bounded capacity full, it persists a non-retryable 403 outcome and replaying that denied job returns the same outcome. Exact replays of an already committed admission reuse its existing reservation. This version has no automatic reservation release: terminal or local decommission state alone does not free a slot. Lease inventory and feature-delivery flags never authorize or deny capacity. Hosted fresh admission also requires the v2-signed commercial runtime and provider entitlements plus the signed `cloud.runtime.credits` `managed_servers` mode/limit decision; feature flags alone never grant provider capacity. Self-host OSS uses its construction-fixed static release-manifest policy instead of a SaaS entitlement dependency.

ionos_datacenter.description: IONOS datacenter alias for provider_region; ignored for other canonical providers.

provider_id.description: Canonical executable provider identifier; historical display aliases are rejected.

provider_region.description: Provider region. For IONOS this is normalized to the canonical datacenter identifier.

runtime_offering_id.description: Canonical managed-runtime offering. Omission uses the stack's snapshotted effective default.

services.description: Service keys; duplicates and order are semantically insignificant.

stackkit.description: StackKit foundation requested for this server.

tools.title: Analyze spec to get requirements (Phase 1)
tools.description: Safe, idempotent. Returns hardware requirements, detected add-ons, required credentials.

tools.title: Apply onboarding action
tools.description: Applies one closed action (complete, skip, dismiss, resume or coach_seen) to the authenticated owner's progress in a journey and answers the resolved journey, state, step availability and revision. Steps that spend money complete only from server facts: a reported completion of such a step is refused with 403 `onboarding_derived_only`. A repeated action is a no-op, and a stale `If-Match` revision answers 412.

if_match.description: Optional compare-and-swap revision read from the journey state, for example `"3"`.

source.description: Who asserts the completion; empty means reported for complete and manual for skip.

step_id.description: Required for complete, skip and coach_seen, for example `techstack.add_server`.

tools.title: Approve pending worker
tools.description: Approve pending worker

tools.title: Approve the key a legacy server proposed
tools.description: Binds the pending key named by `key_thumbprint`, which makes the worker key-bound (bearer-only requests are denied afterwards). Requires the owner and a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old). The approving subject and time are recorded with the identity and logged. 409 `identity_upgrade_not_pending` when no unexpired pending key has that fingerprint.

tools.title: Assign server to stack
tools.description: Binds one approved, connected worker of the owner to one owned stack through the canonical server runtime. A worker that is not approved yet, or that already belongs to another stack, answers 409; assigning it to the stack it already belongs to is a no-op. The body is empty.

tools.title: Attach Home Assistant to its owner
tools.description: Binds the instance's endpoint and the long-lived access token held in the Wallet item `token_wallet_item_id` (a kombify Wallet item assigned to Techstack, or a built-in wallet API key or OAuth token item whose URL names this instance; resolved inside Techstack, never answered; this contract accepts no token) to a pending owner enrollment of an owned stack, with the lifecycle grants and baseline settings the owner chooses. The token is stored encrypted and an existing attachment is never overwritten (409 `attachment_rejected`). Self-hosted installs only (503 otherwise).

lease_id.description: Managed guest lease; required for a new instance.

token_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the Home Assistant long-lived access token.

tools.title: Back up Home Assistant
tools.description: Runs a native full backup through the instance binding, stores it encrypted off the instance and retains the recovery key in custody. Requires an owned instance binding with the backup grant. `operation_id` is a stable identity: repeating it returns the retained result instead of a second backup. A pending operation answers 202.

tools.title: Cancel running scan
tools.description: Cancel running scan

tools.title: Cancel a queued maintenance job
tools.description: Uses the same tenant, entitlement, server and requesting-owner scope as the job read: the authority to withdraw a queued job is the person who owns the server and requested the job, and the person's agent acts with it. No delegated maintenance origin is needed, since cancelling only withdraws work that has not reached the server. Cancellation and execution claim use the same queued-state compare-and-set. Repeating a successful cancellation returns its receipt; a claimed or finished job returns maintenance_not_cancellable. Cancelling never claims to stop a command that has already reached the server.

tools.title: Configure use case
tools.description: Authors a native configuration change for one installed catalog workload (compute, storage and accelerator profiles, public settings, secret references) against the baseline named by `expected_spec_hash`, saves the candidate and queues the StackKit lifecycle jobs that apply it. The `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry replay the original acceptance. Refused with 409 while the stack is busy, a service is locked, a server is in maintenance, or the baseline changed.

expected_spec_hash.description: Native baseline hash read from the use-case configuration view.

secret_refs.description: Existing secret references by catalog key. Values are `secret://` references, never secret material.

settings.description: Public catalog settings by key; each value is a string, boolean or number.

tools.title: Confirm Home Assistant cutover
tools.description: Delivers the explicit cutover confirmation to a migration run that is waiting for it. The run then stops the source, moves the exclusive attachments to the target and starts it; the original and its archive are retained and the migration can be returned with the rollback call. Answers 400 when the run is not awaiting confirmation and 404 for a run the caller does not own.

tools.title: Create action card
tools.description: Stores a card that describes one approved-action primitive, its target and its evidence sink for the authenticated owner. The card starts as `awaiting_grant` (no `grant` given) or `awaiting_approval` and runs nothing until it is approved and executed. The body is decoded strictly and must stay under 64 KiB.

grant.description: Delegated grant binding the card runs under. Without it the card waits for a grant.

operation_class.description: For example product-apply, product-upgrade, product-rollback, mutation or drift-correction.

id.description: Optional card id; generated when omitted.

tools.title: Create a server install command
tools.description: Answers the Linux (and, outside the LAN bridge, Windows) command that installs and enrolls a new server through the current registry URL. Techstack mints the one-time pairing token the command carries (15 minutes) and answers its id and expiry; the token is never an argument.

tools.title: Create a StackKit deployment in the owner's Homelab
tools.description: Creates an internal StackKit deployment under the authenticated B2C owner's singleton Homelab from the canonical StackKits stack-spec payload supplied as `stack_spec`. The legacy `/stacks` route and `stack_id` response field identify that deployment; they do not create or select a second Homelab product. One TechStack instance can serve many owners, each with their own Homelab. Legacy `user_config`/kombination payloads remain accepted at this compatibility boundary. Wizard clients should send a stable `X-Idempotency-Key`; retries with the same key and payload return the original deployment, planned server, and provisioning job.

enable_pocketbase_backend.description: Enable optional PocketBase Homelab backend capabilities

identity_head.description: Homelab identity head selected by Wizard Round 4

user_config.description: Legacy structured configuration, including older kombination-style payloads. New wizard clients should send stack_spec.

tools.title: Create a Home Assistant appliance on a substrate
tools.description: Reserves a guest on a bound substrate (the owner's own Proxmox host, customer custody, local billing, nothing billed by kombify) and submits its creation; the guest is not yet assessed as running (`application_status` is `authenticated_check_pending`). Only the `haos` profile and a placement on this substrate are accepted. The substrate binding must be enabled and its Guard inventory current, and the stack must be owned by the caller. Replaying the same intent with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same guest; a changed intent or a different key for the same stack and node answers 409 `appliance_not_admitted`.

node_id.description: Node the appliance becomes in that stack; one appliance per stack node.

bridge.description: Active LAN bridge name on the substrate.

server_id.description: Must equal the substrate server id in the path.

stack_id.description: Stack that owns the appliance; must belong to the caller.

tools.title: Add wallet item
tools.description: Creates a wallet item owned by the caller in the resolved tenant and returns it redacted. The server assigns the id. `secret` and `totp` values are entered by the person in the Wallet and are not part of this contract; an item created here has no secret until the person adds one, and a secret can never be read back through this API without the person's fresh re-authentication. Only deployments that keep credentials in Techstack's own Wallet serve this route; elsewhere it answers 409 `self_hosted_only`.

kind.description: Defaults to `other`. Cannot be changed later.

notes.description: Free text; never put credentials here.

stack_id.description: Stack (kit deployment) the item belongs to.

tools.title: Run creation wizard
tools.description: Persists one wizard run for the authenticated owner. A found run creates the deployment and its first server, a join run adds a Node and an extend run adds use cases; the first run in a Homelab founds it and later first-run requests are coerced to expansions. The kombify-cloud transport orders a billed managed server, the hypervisor transport creates a guest on the owner's hypervisor and connect-remote enrolls over SSH. Join, extend, managed and hypervisor runs require `X-Idempotency-Key`; a replay with the same key and request returns the original outcome. Requires the `native_v2_wizard` feature for the caller.

intent.description: Closed wizard intent (techstack.wizard-intent/v1). The backend projects it onto the pinned StackKits kit seed; owner identity never travels here.

offsite.description: Off-site object backup; available only when founding a cloud-kit deployment.

goals.description: Selected use-case slugs from the released StackKits catalog.

mode.description: found creates a deployment (kit_slug required); join adds a Node and extend adds use cases to kit_deployment_id.

layout_recommendation.description: Accepts a shown layout recommendation (join and extend runs only).

name.description: Display name of the StackKit deployment.

existing_server_id.description: Already enrolled, unassigned canonical server for the first installation (found runs, install-command transport only).

items.description: controller, worker, storage or edge; the legacy names foundation, standalone, main and control-plane map to controller.

transport.description: Provisioning lane; empty means install-command. kombify-cloud orders a billed managed server.

use_case_capabilities.description: Capability option id (or "off") per capability id, per selected use-case slug.

use_case_settings.description: Setting decisions per selected use-case slug, as the StackKits catalog declares them.

managed.description: Managed provider selection for the kombify-cloud transport.

owner.description: Owner bootstrap options for a first run; ignored on expansion runs.

remote.description: SSH target for the connect-remote transport. The credential is a Wallet node access item; this contract accepts no plaintext password.

ssh_key_label.description: Label of a stored SSH key; only on deployments that read the built-in wallet.

substrate.description: Guest placement on the owner's connected hypervisor; required for, and only valid with, the hypervisor transport.

x_idempotency_key.description: Stable attempt key, at most 256 characters. The handler accepts a missing key only for found runs on the install-command or connect-remote transport.

tools.title: Decommission one StackKit deployment and its infrastructure
tools.description: Removes the stack through its nodes: StackKits removes every applied workload on the server that runs it, then the control plane releases the stack. When a server holding the stack was deleted, the node cannot answer; the request is then refused with `server_absence_confirmation_required` and the offline servers, and is sent again with `offline_removal.confirm_server_ids` naming exactly those servers. The control plane accepts that confirmation only for a server it can prove offline (no heartbeat for longer than the stale window), without a lease and not operated by kombify or a provider: leased and provider-operated servers are proven absent by their provider. A confirmed server is never dispatched to; its agent credential is revoked and the server is retired. A server that reported recently is removed through its node.

confirm_server_ids.description: Every offline server of the stack, by id.

tools.title: Discover a parked provider provision
tools.description: First step of operator resolution for a provision whose outcome is unknown. Reads the provider (read-only) and appends the immutable discovery evidence; it never creates or retries anything at the provider. A replay re-verifies the same observation. The answer names the confirmation string the second step requires. Administrator-only: a non-administrator caller is refused with 403, and the operation must belong to the caller's tenant.

tools.title: Dismiss notification

Techstack signs the call to the notifications engine for the authenticated user, so only that user's own items can be dismissed; an unknown item answers 404. The engine's answer is passed through unchanged and is not wrapped in the `data` envelope.

tools.description: Atomically persists an idempotent, revisioned routing overlay without mutating the user's immutable intent. server_id is always exact and mandatory. lease_id is mandatory for managed runtimes and omitted for a local/Basement runtime which has no lease. For a managed target, a true ensure_rollout request dispatches the existing deploy pipeline only after proving that its selected active foundation lease and canonical Node equal this exact target. The API never reports the resulting job as already applied. The overlay is consumed only while deriving StackKits artifacts and this path never creates or selects a replacement VM.

ensure_rollout.description: Request reconciliation without implying that it has already been dispatched or applied.

A card of operation class `drift-correction` also needs `compensation_card_id`, any other card must not send it. A missing approval or grant, an expired grant and a connector binding that does not match answer 403 or 409 with a stable `reason_code`.

tools.title: Read domain lifecycle and observed DNS/TLS differences
tools.description: Owner and tenant scoped, read-only projection of canonical routing, server domains and service endpoints. Registration expiry from RDAP and certificate expiry from the presented public TLS leaf are separate facts with independent sources and observation deadlines. Missing data stays unknown. Expected DNS is never inferred from observed addresses. Proxied origins are explicitly unobservable from recursive public DNS. Conditions persist across failures and stale observations, and resolve only after fresh positive evidence. An unavailable store returns 503.

tools.title: Read per-drive SMART and NVMe health evidence
tools.description: Authenticated, tenant-scoped projection of Guard drive observations. Self-hosted installations use their configured installation tenant. Hardware identities retain history independently of mutable device paths; replacements never inherit earlier readings. Anonymous observations have attempt-specific IDs and cannot establish historical continuity. Missing, unsupported, inaccessible, incomplete, stale and disconnected observations stay explicit and cannot imply healthy hardware. A server with no observations returns a missing state when selected explicitly. Last successful readings remain historical evidence when a new attempt fails. Only a complete inventory or an explicit missing observation can establish disconnection, and an unreadable identity at a seen path stays uncertain. Reads age evidence and condition episodes, without initiating collection, self-tests, repairs, provisioning or other device actions. Capacity growth forecasts remain on the separate storage-forecast route.

server_id.description: Restrict evidence to one server within the authenticated tenant; an unobserved server remains explicitly missing.

tools.title: Read active and recovered drive-health condition episodes
tools.description: Authenticated, tenant-scoped read of hardware and collection conditions. Each condition names its affected server and, when attributable, immutable drive identity, severity, observed evidence and recommended next step. Collection failures are distinct from hardware diagnoses. Stable episode IDs deduplicate unchanged conditions; resolved_at records recovery only when fresh evidence covers the condition. Anonymous collection incidents deduplicate by server and path, independently of anonymous hardware IDs. Nonzero cumulative counters describe historical totals; measured increases are separate conditions. NVMe command-error increases and consumed rated endurance are advisories, rather than standalone evidence of media failure. Resolved history is bounded to 64 episodes per condition scope and 90 days. Reads initiate no repair, device mutation or provider action.

server_id.description: Restrict evidence to one server within the authenticated tenant; an unobserved server remains explicitly missing.

tools.title: Project filesystem growth from observed storage gauges
tools.description: Read-only, tenant-scoped projection of node_disk_used_bytes with contemporaneous node_disk_total_bytes or used plus free bytes. The latter is effective usable capacity, not physical disk capacity. Uses a 14-day window with hourly query evaluation, retaining actual source observation times and deduplicating repeated lookback values. Counts describe hourly sampled observations, not all ingested samples; sparse observations outside the backend lookback may be absent. No interpolation or per-service storage attribution is performed. Separate origin/source streams remain separate resources and are never summed. Guard OTLP times describe Guard collection, not original OTLP point time. Unknown capacity, stale/inadequate history and inconsistent measurements return an explicit state without an exhaustion estimate. Exhaustion is a growth scenario range measured from the latest observation, not a statistical confidence interval. Both bounded queries share a timeout.

This read-only endpoint never calls a provider or a runtime agent and never returns provider resource handles, commands, evidence documents, or credentials. A terminal operation is no longer running, but is not by itself proof of successful cleanup: provider absence requires absence_evidence_ref, and capacity release requires capacity_released.

tools.title: Show whether a server still needs its identity key approved
tools.description: For the owner of the worker. `identity_binding=legacy_bearer` with `code=guard_identity_upgrade_required` means the server authenticates with its bearer credential alone and is observe-only; `pending` carries the fingerprint of the key the server proposed, which the owner compares with the fingerprint the Guard logs on the server. A worker of another tenant or owner is 404.

tools.title: Link an existing Home Assistant
tools.description: Probes a Home Assistant instance from a local executor with the long-lived access token held in the Wallet item `token_wallet_item_id` (a kombify Wallet item assigned to Techstack, or a built-in wallet API key or OAuth token item whose URL names this instance; resolved inside Techstack, never answered) and records a read-only observed service. This contract accepts no token. The token is used for this probe only and is never stored in the registry row. Self-hosted installs only (503 `lan_executor_unavailable` otherwise). The call is idempotent: an already linked instance returns `existing: true` without a new probe.

token_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the Home Assistant long-lived access token.

tools.title: Record an existing service
tools.description: Adds an observed (unmanaged) service row for a server of an owned stack. The row is keyed by stack, server and service name, so repeating the call updates the same row. Nothing is deployed or probed. Either `name` or `service_id` is required and is normalized to a lower-case key. A stack the caller does not own is refused with 403 and an unknown stack or server with 404.

name.description: Service name; used when `service_id` is not set.

server_id.description: Registry server (node) id of the stack.

service_id.description: Service key; used only when `name` is not set.

type.description: Service type, for example `media`; defaults to `custom`.

tools.title: Import stack-spec.yaml as a StackKit deployment
tools.description: Imports YAML or JSON as a deployment under the authenticated owner's Homelab.

tools.title: Install missing host dependencies
tools.description: Installs the missing host dependencies (OpenTofu, cloudflared, Docker) on the machine a self-hosted Techstack runs on, all of them or the named ones. Only the owner of a self-hosted Techstack may call it, and an agent acts with the owner's reach there; hosted Techstack refuses every caller with 403 `host_install_unavailable` (reason_code `hosted_control_plane`) before anything is detected.

dependencies.description: Names of the missing dependencies to install; all when omitted.

tools.title: Run a PromQL instant query
tools.description: Run a PromQL instant query

tools.title: Invite household member
tools.description: Invites one person of the household plan to the owned stack. The person must match the persisted Wizard intent (`client_ref`, e-mail and display name), the owner must already be active on the stack, and the body must carry `owner_approved: true`. The body is decoded strictly. The response includes the member's activation URL when one exists.

client_ref.description: Reference of the planned person in the Wizard household intent.

tools.title: Issue owner activation link
tools.description: Asks the StackKits identity runtime of the owned stack for a link that activates the owner's own account on the stack. The body must carry `owner_approved: true`; any other body is 400 `owner_approval_required`. The response includes the activation URL, which is a one-time sign-in link: hand it to the owner and do not log it. Answers 409 when the pinned StackKits runtime cannot issue activations or issuing fails.

tools.title: List the tenant's failure resolution outcomes
tools.description: Returns the caller tenant's own recorded resolution outcomes, newest first, and the succeeded and failed counts per resolution and signature. Another tenant's outcomes are never visible.

tools.title: List the tenant's failure signatures
tools.description: Returns the caller tenant's own failed operations normalized into failure signatures, most recently seen first. A signature is the SHA-256 over the normalizer version, component, phase, error code and a template in which every variable token (timestamps, IDs, addresses, host names, paths, user names, quoted values, numbers) is replaced. No raw error text is stored or returned, and another tenant's occurrences are never visible.

window_days.description: Length of the growth window; recent_occurrences counts the last window, previous_occurrences the one before it.

tools.title: List all features grouped by category
tools.description: List all features grouped by category

tools.title: List the unresolved operation outcomes of one kombify Guard
tools.description: Lists the operations of an owned worker whose outcome is unknown: the kombify Guard recorded that the effect may or may not have happened and no observation settled it. Each one fences further changes on the server. `state` is `reconciling` while the Guard still tries to settle it and `needs_operator` once it stayed unresolved past the configured time (`TECHSTACK_GUARD_OUTCOME_NEEDS_OPERATOR_AFTER`, default 30 minutes). The time only changes how the outcome is shown; it never releases the fence. Another tenant's or owner's worker is 404.

tools.title: List jobs owned by the authenticated user
tools.description: Returns the same owner-scoped job state used by the operator UI and automation clients. A job with `state: waiting` remains active and the current orchestrator process schedules its next check; it is not a failed provider action. If that schedule becomes stale after a process restart, use the exact-target `resumeStackEnrollment` operation.

service_id.description: Return only jobs whose recorded service target matches this id.

state.description:
`waiting` is active, non-terminal work. Clients must keep polling or
consuming SSE and must not enable target access until completion.

tools.title: List the owner's StackKit deployments
tools.description: Returns every StackKit deployment beneath the authenticated owner's singleton B2C Homelab. `kit_deployment_id`, `homelab_id`, and `stackkit_id` are the product identities; legacy identifiers remain compatibility aliases on this route while consumers migrate.

tools.description: Returns owner-scoped Nodes with canonical `node_id` and `kit_deployment_id` identities.

tools.title: List the open findings and recent findings history of one server
tools.description: The findings ledger behind the server's `security`, `recovery` and Guard alerts. One finding is one episode: opened when a fact is first observed wrong, resolved when it is observed right again, with at most one alert (`alerted_at`) and one resolution. History is kept 90 days.

tools.description: List the recent security repairs of one server

tools.title: List servers
tools.description: Returns only servers owned by the authenticated subject in the trusted tenant context. Tenant and owner overrides are not accepted. Raw metadata, channel endpoints, provider-resource references, credentials, SSH material, tokens, and logs are never returned. The lease projection contains only an opaque identifier and state. Cursor pages share one authorization- and filter-bound collection watermark and exclude later inserts. Each server carries its connection and health state and a freshness-qualified metrics block (cpu, memory and disk percent, uptime seconds); a figure from a stale heartbeat is reported as stale without a value.

tools.description: List sanitized services for the authenticated owner's servers

cursor.description: Opaque cursor bound to the authenticated scope and exact server_id filter.

server_id.description: Optional exact owned server filter; a foreign server is returned as not found.

tools.title: List available StackKits
tools.description: List available StackKits

tools.title: List explicit primary routing targets for one StackKit deployment
tools.description: Read-only discovery backed by active RuntimeLease authority. Returns every owner-visible foundation/control-plane target and never selects one, creates a canonical Node (`ServerRuntime`) projection, or mutates the StackKit deployment. Callers must send the complete server_id and lease_id tuple to a routing mutation.

tools.description: List services under one of the caller's own kombify.me base subdomains

tools.description: Requires an authenticated caller. With the shared platform identity the list is scoped to the caller's owner binding.

tools.title: List redacted wallet recovery items
tools.description: Lists the caller's wallet recovery items for the resolved tenant. The `secret` and `totp` values are always stripped from this response; only presence flags (`has_secret`, `has_totp`) are exposed.

tools.title: List server key approvals waiting for the owner
tools.description: For the owner. Each entry is a server of theirs that proposed a key and is observe-only until that exact key is approved with `approveWorkerIdentityUpgrade` (fresh multi-factor sign-in required). Entries carry the hostname and the key fingerprint to compare with the one the Guard logs on the server. Listing grants nothing.

tools.title: List registered workers (filtered by owner)
tools.description: List registered workers (filtered by owner)

tools.title: Mark all notifications read
tools.description: Marks all unread items of the authenticated user's notification feed as read, across every section. The body is empty. The engine's answer is passed through unchanged and is not wrapped in the `data` envelope.

tools.title: Mark notification read
tools.description: Marks one item of the authenticated user's notification feed as read. Techstack signs the call to the notifications engine for the authenticated user, so only that user's own items can be changed; an unknown item answers 404. The engine's answer is passed through unchanged and is not wrapped in the `data` envelope.

tools.title: Move a service to another server
tools.description: Marks the source service as migrating, creates the target copy pending verification and starts a migration job. The target server must belong to the same stack and differ from the source, and the service must be movable. Today every call answers 501 `Runtime service migration is unavailable` (`migration_available` is false in the registry) until a runtime executor exists; the canonical inventory store additionally answers 503 `service_control_server_fence_unavailable`.

tools.title: Verify request-bound managed-runtime authority without creating a resource
tools.description: Read-only preflight for the Gateway-to-native-admission authority chain. Hosted requests must carry the Gateway's v2-signed managed-runtime, Cloud Kit, provider entitlement, and `cloud.runtime.credits` `managed_servers` decision bound to this exact request. A successful response never reserves capacity or creates a StackKit deployment, queue job, lease, Node projection, or provider operation; the real Add-Server request repeats every mutable admission check atomically.

provider_id.description: Exact canonical provider whose managed-runtime authority is being checked.

tools.title: Assess one exact existing Home Assistant Container for in-place adoption
tools.description: Retains the source-bound assessment in the existing durable job store. Requires a connected Guard and the exact capable published CLI release. This read-only operation does not establish Stacked membership.

tools.title: Prepare a device
tools.description: Connects to the named machine over SSH, runs the named catalog resolutions in order (only catalog ids are accepted), optionally opens a temporary egress path while they run, and probes again to report the result. Requires the signed techstack.device.prepare entitlement, and techstack.device.egress when egress is true. Registered only on a local (non-SaaS) control plane. The login comes from the Wallet item connection.wallet_item_id, resolved inside Techstack for this request only. A failing resolution stops the run with 409 and the receipts collected so far.

host_key_fingerprint.description: Key the device must present; omit on the first request.

wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password; this contract accepts no key, passphrase or password.

egress.description: Open a temporary way out for the machine while the fixes run.

interface.description: Interface a fix should act on, when one asks for it.

tools.title: Preview pipeline results without side effects
tools.description: Safe, idempotent. Shows what would be generated. Backend validation or StackKit resolution failures return 200 with data.valid=false and structured data.errors; malformed input and auth failures remain HTTP errors.

tools.title: Preview wizard spec
tools.description: Projects a wizard intent onto the pinned kit seed and validates the result with the pinned StackKits CLI. Safe and idempotent: nothing is persisted. An invalid projection answers 200 with `valid: false` and `validate_error`; join previews need `base_spec`. Requires the `native_v2_wizard` feature for the caller (403 `feature_not_enabled` otherwise).

base_spec.description: Current spec of the deployment being joined; required for join previews.

intent.description: Closed wizard intent (techstack.wizard-intent/v1). The backend projects it onto the pinned StackKits kit seed; owner identity never travels here.

offsite.description: Off-site object backup; available only when founding a cloud-kit deployment.

goals.description: Selected use-case slugs from the released StackKits catalog.

mode.description: found creates a deployment (kit_slug required); join adds a Node and extend adds use cases to kit_deployment_id.

layout_recommendation.description: Accepts a shown layout recommendation (join and extend runs only).

name.description: Display name of the StackKit deployment.

existing_server_id.description: Already enrolled, unassigned canonical server for the first installation (found runs, install-command transport only).

items.description: controller, worker, storage or edge; the legacy names foundation, standalone, main and control-plane map to controller.

transport.description: Provisioning lane; empty means install-command. kombify-cloud orders a billed managed server.

use_case_capabilities.description: Capability option id (or "off") per capability id, per selected use-case slug.

use_case_settings.description: Setting decisions per selected use-case slug, as the StackKits catalog declares them.

tools.title: Check a device is ready
tools.description: Opens one SSH session to the named machine, reads its facts (network, proxy, virtualization, enrollment reachability) and answers a readiness report; nothing on the device changes. The login comes from the Wallet item connection.wallet_item_id, resolved inside Techstack for this request only and never answered or stored. Registered only on a local (non-SaaS) control plane and requires the signed techstack.device.prepare entitlement. Unknown body fields are refused. The first request may omit host_key_fingerprint; the answer then carries the key the device presented so it can be pinned on the next call.

host_key_fingerprint.description: Key the device must present; omit on the first request.

wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password; this contract accepts no key, passphrase or password.

tools.title: Probe a discovered device
tools.description: Logs in to the device over SSH with the login held in the Wallet item `ssh_wallet_item_id` (a kombify Wallet node access item assigned to Techstack and bound to this IP or to no host, or an SSH key or password item of the built-in wallet whose URL names this IP) and reads its system facts. The login is resolved inside Techstack for this probe only and never answered. This contract accepts no password or private key. Non-admin callers may only probe IPs from their own discovery results; admins may probe arbitrary IPs. Local control planes only (409 `lan_executor_required` on a hosted one).

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.title: Start provisioning an existing StackKit deployment
tools.description: Start provisioning an existing StackKit deployment

tools.title: Run a PromQL range query
tools.description: Run a PromQL range query

tools.title: Read the retained application assessment and durable progress
tools.description: Read the retained application assessment and durable progress

tools.title: Read node-owned connector status and current published transport admission
tools.description: Returns a secret-free projection. An unavailable supporting catalog remains nondispatchable SourcePreview; stale evidence on a supporting pin requires current read-only verification. Dispatchability additionally requires current canonical host-key, node and lease authority.

tools.title: Re-bind a moved server to the network it is on now
tools.description: Runs `stackkit network rebind` on the server through its kombify Guard: the node re-detects its LAN address, re-issues the signed LAN DNS custody record and regenerates and re-applies the workspace. The request takes no body. Requires the owner, the Inventory operate grant and the `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement, and a connected Guard (409 `server_network_not_ready` otherwise). A rebind that is already queued or running answers with its job instead of queueing another.

tools.title: Recommend layout
tools.description: Plans where the selected goals run across the nodes of one owned StackKit deployment for an add-server or add-use-case change, verifies the option with the pinned StackKits feasibility check and, when it is feasible, records it as an open recommendation the owner can accept inside a wizard run, reject or snooze. An option that is not verified is returned with state `unverified` and no id. Records the proposal but changes no infrastructure.

planned_node.description: The node an add-server run brings, when its size is known before it enrolls.

tools.title: Recommend StackKits
tools.description: Computes ranked StackKit recommendations from the selected goals, the deployment lane and surface, and the authenticated owner's worker inventory and self-disclosure. Safe and idempotent: nothing is stored. A non-ready status (`incomplete`, `stale`, `degraded`) is still a useful answer that names the evidence to supply.

available_goals.description: Use cases the released catalog offers.

selection_intent.description: all asks which of available_goals the full-homelab template should preselect.

tools.title: Recover the Guard session of a managed runtime
tools.description: Probes the canonical aggregate; when it cannot prove a Guard connection, restarts Guard over the pinned execution channel for an entitled owner of a running server and re-observes the connection within a bounded window, then converges enrollment to enrolled. A stopped runtime is refused (managed_runtime_stopped). No provider resource is touched.

tools.title: Record the outcome of an applied failure resolution
tools.description: Attributes a finished procedure job of the caller tenant to the failure resolution it applied and the failure signature it was applied to. The outcome is the job's terminal state (completed is succeeded, failed is failed), never a value the caller sends; a job that is still running or was canceled is refused. The context is the one of the tenant's own latest occurrence of that signature. The record stays in the tenant; repeating the call for the same resolution and job returns the stored record.

job_id.description: The tenant's job that ran the procedure.

procedure.description: Product procedure reference of the applied fix step.

resolution_id.description: Id of the failure resolution that was applied (find_similar_failures).

signature.description: Failure signature the resolution was applied to; the tenant must have an occurrence of it.

tools.title: Recreate one fully released managed server generation
tools.description: Explicitly provisions generation N+1 for the same provider-neutral runtime slot after generation N has terminal lease and canonical server state, terminal provider operation state, opaque provider-native absence evidence, and exact capacity release. The immutable provider, region, offering, role, StackKit, and service intent is recovered from the old owner-scoped lease; clients cannot replace it. The endpoint delegates to the same managed-runtime expansion authority as Add Node, so enrollment, Guard evidence, endpoints, and StackKit rollout proceed through the full Creation flow. A standard Idempotency-Key is mandatory and safely replays the accepted generation.

confirmed.description: Explicit acknowledgement that Recreate provisions and bills a new managed server generation.

tools.title: Reject layout recommendation
tools.description: Marks an open or snoozed layout recommendation of the authenticated owner as rejected so it is no longer offered, and answers its updated view. A recommendation in any other state answers 409 `layout_recommendation_changed`.

tools.title: Release an adopted lifecycle binding without deleting or stopping its runtime
tools.description: Release an adopted lifecycle binding without deleting or stopping its runtime

tools.title: Remove/deregister agent
tools.description: Remove/deregister agent

tools.title: Remove Cloud link
tools.description: Deletes the stored kombify Cloud profile link of the authenticated operator on this install. The link is per operator; nothing at kombify Cloud changes. When no link exists the call succeeds with `removed: false`. Re-linking is a browser sign-in and is not available to agents.

tools.title: Remove use case
tools.description: Retires an installed workload, or every installed workload of a catalog use case, through the native resolver against the baseline named by `expected_spec_hash`, and queues the StackKit lifecycle jobs. The workload stops running but its data is retained (`data_disposition: retain`). The `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry replay the original acceptance; refused with 409 while the stack is busy, a service is locked or a server is in maintenance.

expected_spec_hash.description: Native baseline hash read from the use-case configuration view.

selector_ref.description: Workload slug or catalog use-case id; no surrounding whitespace.

tools.title: Rename homelab
tools.description: Renames the authenticated owner's homelab. The homelab name is the Stack Identity name and syncs to kombify Cloud when connected. Reversible; the homelab is resolved from the authenticated owner, never from an argument.

tools.title: Rename server
tools.description: Writes servers.display_name, which runtime projections never overwrite. `null` or an empty string clears the rename. Requires the signed techstack.inventory.write entitlement and the FGA server `caller` relation; the write is bound to the authenticated tenant and owner, and a server outside that scope is denied without revealing whether it exists. The canonical inventory `name` reports the chosen name when one is set.

tools.title: Prepare the pairing command that re-pairs this server
tools.description: Issues a one-time install command for a server whose Guard pinned no binding signing key. The token is returned once. Mutating commands stay refused until the server is paired again.

tools.title: Repair one degraded component of a completed rollout on its existing server
tools.description: A rollout whose stack core applied completes degraded when an independent component could not finish; the component is recorded in the stack's `degraded_components` and repaired automatically. This operation starts that repair now. `public_tls` installs the managed kombify.me origin certificate (ADR-0047) on the stack's server; its hostnames come from the degraded rollout, never from the request. Answers 409 `component_repair_not_needed` when nothing is degraded.

tools.title: Restart onboarding
tools.description: Clears the authenticated owner's completed and seen steps in a journey and reactivates it so the tour is shown again. Only the owner's own progress changes; no infrastructure is touched. Answers the resolved journey like the action route.

tools.title: Trigger drift resolution (re-apply)
tools.description: Precondition -- stack must have status "drifted"

tools.title: Archive a legacy or unbound custody record after provider cleanup
tools.description: Removes a non-executable legacy or unbound lease from the active dashboard only after the owner confirms that its provider resource was already removed. This operation never contacts or deletes a provider resource and is rejected for Techstack provider-controlled generations.

tools.title: Resolve a parked provider provision
tools.description: Second step of operator resolution. With the exact confirmation from the discovery step it appends one decision against the persisted observation: no candidate, adopt the single exact candidate, or quarantine several. The decision is local custody state and never starts or retries provider creation. Replays return the original decision. Administrator-only; a stale or mismatching observation answers 409.

confirmation.description: Must equal required_confirmation from the discovery step (adopt-provision:<operationId>).

operation_id.description: Provider operation id (non-empty, at most 256 characters, no whitespace or control characters).

tools.title: Resolve workload relocation
tools.description: Re-reads the transfer proof from the source and destination nodes of one relocation and records the verified outcome (`moved` or `aborted`). It is used when a move stopped between transfer and verification. The body is empty. While the nodes cannot both prove the exact transfer the answer is 409 and the relocation stays fenced.

tools.title: Restore Home Assistant to a recovery instance
tools.description: Restores a completed retained backup into the isolated recovery binding that belongs to the instance and verifies the result; the running instance itself is not overwritten. Requires the restore grant and an owned recovery binding (403 `recovery_not_authorized` otherwise). `operation_id` is a stable identity. A pending operation answers 202.

tools.title: Retry remote SSH enrollment
tools.description: Re-runs the Guard enrollment over the SSH connection persisted for a connect-remote deployment without rerunning the StackKit rollout. The deployment must belong to the authenticated owner and use the connect-remote transport; the credential comes from the Wallet node access item already bound to it, or from `ssh_wallet_item_id` when the connection should be rebound first. A plaintext password is never accepted by this contract.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet node access item to rebind the stack's persisted SSH connection to before the retry.

tools.title: Resume one overdue managed Node wait on its exact existing VM
tools.description: Authenticated, idempotent recovery for a persisted `waiting_enrollment`, `waiting_provider_provision`, or `waiting_canonical_guard` job whose `next_resume_at` has been overdue beyond the bounded grace period. The server validates the owned StackKit deployment, source job, wait reason, exact lease, active foundation role, and canonical Node as one operation. It atomically retires the exact source wait, creates or rehydrates one deterministic replacement deploy bound to the same lease and Node, and replays that job on later calls. Before handler entry, queue workers atomically acquire the durable `tenant/stack` compatibility execution claim; this serializes different jobs for the same StackKit deployment across Techstack replicas. The claim remains durable `running` until the handler exits, including during cancellation. This endpoint never invokes provider VM creation or selects a newer VM. A replacement found durable `running` after a crash remains fail-closed, is reported as the same job, and is never duplicated automatically; runtime-action reconciliation remains a separate operator concern.

job_id.description: Persisted source job currently projected as waiting_enrollment.

lease_id.description: Exact managed foundation lease already bound to the source job.

tools.title: Retry one failed StackKit deployment rollout on its exact existing managed VM
tools.description: Validates the owned failed deploy, its exact active foundation lease, and canonical Node in one server-side operation. The deterministic durable replacement bypasses provider VM creation, wins a durable `tenant/stack` compatibility execution claim before handler entry, and is replayed on repeated calls to this operation. The claim serializes different jobs for the same StackKit deployment across replicas and remains fail-closed as `running` after a process crash until operator reconciliation.

candidate_spec.description: Optional canonical StackSpec repairing missing route, access and data dependencies of already admitted modules. The pinned CLI validates it; revision CAS and candidate digest bind retries. Applied installations must use their existing change-set authority.

current_spec_hash.description: Normalized current node intent hash for an exact failed INIT whose immutable retry lineage proves a prior failed APPLY on this runtime. Required only for that partial INIT recovery; rejected on other paths. This is solely the CLI atomic CAS precondition, never authorization. Obtain through the pinned CLI resolve on the same current canonical node document. The durable receipt seals this value and lineage against changed replay.

lease_id.description: Exact active managed foundation lease bound to the failed job.

owner_approved.description: Required true when supplying a canonical initial-rollout repair candidate.

source_job_id.description: Exact failed deploy job used as immutable retry evidence.

tools.title: Review or apply owner-scoped test-residue cleanup
tools.description: Two-phase cleanup for control-plane projections only. A `dry_run` returns the exact authenticated-owner E2E/runtime-cloud candidates and a stable revision-bound digest. `apply` recomputes the plan and accepts only that exact digest. This route never decommissions a lease, calls a provider, destroys infrastructure, or enqueues lifecycle work.

digest.description: Required for apply; copied unchanged from the reviewed dry-run.

stack_id.description: Optional exact deployment scope used by E2E cleanup.

tools.title: Return Home Assistant migration
tools.description: Starts the return run for an owned migration that completed or failed and kept its source archive: archive the target, stop it, return the exclusive attachments and start and verify the original. The return run id is the migration run id with `:rollback`, so repeating the call resumes it. Answers 400 when the migration is not in a returnable state and 404 for a run the caller does not own.

tools.title: Queue an owner-authorized StackKits service action
tools.description: Derives stack, server, agent, kit and service authority from fresh canonical inventory. Exact replays converge through a durable job receipt; the raw Idempotency-Key is never persisted. Mutations are followed by StackKits verify before measured state changes. Agent-executed actions refuse with 409 `maintenance_active` while the server is being rebooted or updated.

body.description: Either an agent-executed runtime action bound to a fresh inventory revision, or an owner lock action executed entirely in the control plane. The lock is not bound to an inventory observation: an owner must be able to freeze a service whose agent is unreachable.

action.description: `update` runs the StackKit upgrade of the owning stack to the pinned release; it is accepted only while `allowed_actions` advertises it.

cursor.description: Logs only; opaque StackKits cursor from the prior page.

owner_approved.description: Required true for start, stop and restart; logs is read-only.

oneOf.description: Asserts or clears the owner mutation lock. Applied synchronously by the control plane, so the response carries no job id and reports status `completed`. Repeating the same lock state is a no-op.

owner_approved.description: Required true; changing a guardrail is an owner decision.

tools.title: Run full unifier pipeline (validate + analyze + unify + generate)
tools.description: Side-effecting -- generates IaC output files.

tools.title: Queue an owned server OS update plan, OS update or reboot
tools.description: Requires the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, and current server-bound standing authority for delegated native MCP calls. These three ordinary actions require no fresh MFA or separate owner_approved assertion. Reboot and os_update require expected_impact_digest from the preview the user confirmed. Impact is compared atomically at admission and again at execution claim; changed or incomplete evidence sends no command and requires a refreshed preview and renewed confirmation with a new request key. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys, no duplicates, no unknown fields. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored receipt before target validation. One reboot or OS update and, separately, one update plan may be active per server; a job not finished by its deadline fails with `deadline_exceeded` and frees its slot. The action is offered in `allowed_actions` only when the server agent advertises `stackkit.host-maintenance.v1`, and `reboot` only when the server also reports `host_boot_id`. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of control_plane_host, substrate_node, protected_demo_server, service_locked, maintenance_active, node_operation_active, plan_stale, agent_capability_missing, boot_id_unknown, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, inventory_revision_stale, idempotency_key_reused, impact_confirmation_required, impact_changed or impact_unavailable; 403 carries entitlement_required or maintenance_origin_authority_denied.

expected_impact_digest.description: Required for os_update and reboot, forbidden for os_update_plan. snapshot_digest of the current impact preview confirmed for this exact server and action. Changing it under an existing Idempotency-Key is a conflict; a renewed confirmation uses a new key.

expected_plan_digest.description: os_update only: the plan_digest of a completed os_update_plan for this server that is at most 15 minutes old.

owner_approved.description: Optional legacy field; it does not grant maintenance authority.

tools.title: Run an admitted StackKit operation
tools.description: Uses the same tenant- and owner-scoped dispatcher as the operator UI. The node executes through its authenticated channel, current release pin, native Advanced catalog and issued operation capability. Techstack never executes Terramate, apply, rollback, backup or restore itself. A mutation requires owner_approved; service locks and active server maintenance are checked before enqueue. Direct backup_run and backup_configure remain Basement-only; managed kits keep their schedule and sealed target-renewal authority. backup_configure derives the node's target and plan from existing custody and accepts no credential fields. advanced_change_set requires candidate_spec; rollback requires an exact rollback_target_ref; restore_drill may reuse a snapshot_anchor_id. ai_provider lets Private AI offer an external OpenAI-compatible provider: the kombify Wallet seals the item wallet_item_id (the provider's API key) to the node, which must be listed as a host target of that item, the node binds it to ai_provider_base_url, and a drift reconcile applies the setting. ai_provider_disable removes it. ssh_trust_recipient and ssh_trust_apply let the server trust the owner's kombify Wallet SSH CA: ssh_trust_recipient has the node answer the owner's recipient_challenge with its owner-signed recipient statement and returns it with the host target the owner lists on the CA item; the owner then asks the Wallet for the ssh-ca-trust delivery and ssh_trust_apply hands its sealed_delivery to the node, which installs TrustedUserCAKeys and the principals of each local user. Restore activation requires exactly one Idempotency-Key header, while other operations have no replay guarantee. Acceptance is not execution success; read the returned job and its scoped result to observe effects.

ai_provider_base_url.description: https base URL of the OpenAI-compatible provider API for ai_provider.

ai_provider_disable.description: Remove the external provider instead of setting it.

candidate_spec.description: Canonical candidate StackSpec validated by the pinned node executor; required for advanced_change_set.

recipient_challenge.description: The owner's fresh challenge the node's recipient statement answers; ssh_trust_recipient only.

rollback_target_ref.description: Exact executor-state snapshot or change-set digest.

sealed_delivery.description: The kombify Wallet's sealed ssh-ca-trust, ssh-ca-revoke or ssh-host-certificate envelope (JSON text, public material only); ssh_trust_apply only.

stackkit.description: Optional execution binding; normally derived from the stack's managed rollout.

wallet_item_id.description: kombify Wallet item holding the provider's API key for ai_provider.

wallet_item_rotate.description: Deliver a rotated item that replaces the version the node holds.

tools.description: Send command to agent

tools.title: Get server access context
tools.description: Returns address metadata, channel state, and freshness-qualified service links only. It never returns endpoint references, access-profile references, route IDs, credentials, tokens, SSH users, ports, keys, commands, or logs. This surface requires inventory operate permission; read permission alone is insufficient.

tools.title: Get server health
tools.description: Get freshness-qualified health for one owned server

tools.title: Get server ports
tools.description: Projects compiler-declared listener claims and generation-fenced reservations beside monotone Guard runtime evidence. Missing or stale observations remain explicit and never become optimistic availability.

tools.title: Set notification preferences
tools.description: Writes the topic-by-channel preference matrix of the authenticated user. Techstack forwards the body (at most 1 MiB) to the notifications engine unchanged; the engine rejects unknown topics and channels with 400 and silently ignores channels that are locked for a topic. The answer is the fresh matrix, not wrapped in the `data` envelope. Quiet hours and the Telegram link are read-only here.

only_if_unset.description: When true, a channel the user already set is left as it is.

channels.description: Channel name (email, in_app, slack, sms, push, telegram) to its new state.

tools.title: Set operator self-disclosure
tools.description: Replaces the signed-in operator's whole self-disclosure; an unanswered question means "not told". The body is decoded strictly and every answer must come from the closed vocabulary below. The capability profile in the answer is derived by the Unifier, never stored from the request. With `if_unchanged` the replacement is applied only when the stored value still equals it, otherwise the answer is 412 `self_disclosure_changed`.

if_unchanged.description: The stored value this replacement must still match.

source.description: link when the answers arrived as URL state and the operator confirmed them; techstack when typed in a Techstack surface.

tools.title: Confirm server availability
tools.description: The owner says whether the machine is on all the time (`always-on`) or switched off at times (`part-time`). The statement is stored next to what the Guard observed and replaces the observed class for planning. `unknown` or `null` withdraws it. Owner only; any other caller gets 404.

class.description: always-on or part-time confirms; unknown or null withdraws the confirmation.

tools.title: Enable or disable a substrate binding
tools.description: Binds the substrate to the Guard's current authenticated inventory (node, guest-id range, image pins) and turns guest placement on or off. Optimistic concurrency: `revision` must equal the current binding revision (0 when none exists) and the answer carries the next one. Refused with 409 while the substrate has no current inventory, no node-local configuration, a revision mismatch, or non-decommissioned guests that still hold custody.

revision.description: Current binding revision; 0 creates the binding.

tools.title: Ensure or revoke one declared owned Home Assistant connector on its node
tools.description: Requires fresh backend ownership, positive operate authority, exact current inventory and Owner approval. Transports only closed correlation metadata through Guard to the published pinned CLI, whose local signedApply and Owner setup authority remain mandatory. Stores pre-send durable intent; unknown acknowledgement only reconciles the original operation read-only. Current v0.51.8 lacks the supporting catalog and returns nondispatchable SourcePreview. Credentials stay in node custody.

tools.title: Snooze layout recommendation
tools.description: Hides an open or snoozed layout recommendation of the authenticated owner until `until`, which must lie in the future and within 90 days, and answers its updated view. A recommendation in any other state answers 409 `layout_recommendation_changed`.

until.description: End of the snooze, at most 90 days ahead.

tools.title: Start Home Assistant migration
tools.description: Starts (or resumes) the durable migration run for an authorized local binding: archive the source, provision an isolated target on the owner's own substrate, restore and verify it, then wait for the cutover confirmation. The run id is derived from tenant, owner and target, so repeating the call resumes the same run. The request must match the binding's source service and authorization reference exactly (403 otherwise). Self-hosted installs with a configured local binding only (503 `migration_executor_unavailable` otherwise).

authorization_ref.description: Opaque reference of the binding's authorization; not a secret.

tools.title: Start a stopped managed server of the same generation
tools.description: Admits one generation-bound provider-control reconcile toward running. The provider power-on runs once under an at-most-once claim; a repeated request while it converges replays the same operation. Requires the managed runtime entitlement before any provider call.

tools.title: Start network scan (async)
tools.description: Start network scan (async)

tools.title: Start Cloudflare tunnel
tools.description: Start Cloudflare tunnel

tools.title: Move workloads to another server
tools.description: Starts a verified move of workloads from the source server (this stack, `source_agent_id`) to a destination server of another owned stack. The workloads stop on the source while they transfer and the source is kept until both nodes verify the transfer; it can be resumed with the abort operation. Select either whole `projects` or individual `resource_uuids`. The transfer secret stays in Wallet custody (`wallet_item_id`) and domain switches go only to test domains. Needs exactly one Idempotency-Key; a replay returns the same job. Refused with 409 when a target holds locked services or server maintenance runs.

destination_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the destination server; must differ from the source.

items.description: OLD=NEW host names; NEW must be a test domain.

projects.description: Whole Coolify projects to move. Mutually exclusive with resource_uuids.

resource_uuids.description: Individual Coolify resources to move. Mutually exclusive with projects.

source_agent_id.description: Guard agent of the source server in this stack.

wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item id (itm_...) of the transfer secret; never the secret itself.

tools.title: Stop a managed server without destroying it
tools.description: Admits one generation-bound provider-control reconcile toward stopped. centron uses its graceful guest shutdown action; IONOS shuts the guest down over the execution channel because the IONOS provider stop releases the bound DHCP IPv4. The server keeps its disk, address, lease, capacity reservation and monthly billing.

tools.title: Stop Cloudflare tunnel
tools.description: Stop Cloudflare tunnel

tools.title: Sync stack identity with Cloud
tools.description: Takes the kombify Cloud stack identity record (read by the caller through the Gateway with the user's own token; `null` when Cloud has none) and applies the sync rules to the local copy: adopt the Cloud record, confirm an identical one, or answer the body to push to Cloud with the `If-Match` revision. The call itself never writes to Cloud. When no local stack identity exists yet it only reports `homelab_missing`.

cloud.description: The Cloud record, or null when Cloud has no stack identity.

tools.title: Test SSH to a discovered device
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection with the login held in the Wallet item `ssh_wallet_item_id` (its key when it holds one, otherwise its password; a built-in wallet item must name this IP as its URL), resolved inside Techstack and never answered; nothing is stored. This contract accepts no password. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false`. Non-admin callers may only test IPs from their own discovery results; admins may test arbitrary IPs. Local control planes only.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.title: Test remote SSH
tools.description: Opens one SSH connection to the given host with a credential held in the Wallet and reports whether it succeeded; nothing is stored. The credential is a Wallet node access item (`ssh_wallet_item_id`, bound to the host) or, on deployments that read the built-in wallet, the label of a stored SSH key. This contract accepts no password or private key. A failed connection answers 200 with `success: false` and the error. Requires the `native_v2_wizard` feature for the caller.

ssh_key_label.description: Label of a stored SSH key; only on deployments that read the built-in wallet.

ssh_wallet_item_id.description: Wallet node access item holding the SSH key or password.

tools.title: Unify specifications (Phase 2)
tools.description: Unify specifications (Phase 2)

tools.title: Update Home Assistant
tools.description: Updates the instance to the exact `version`. It requires a completed backup (`backup_operation_id`) whose archive passed an isolated restore, the update grant on the binding and a pinned version (core `YYYY.M.P`, os `M.N` or `M.N.P`). `operation_id` is a stable identity and an uncertain submission is never repeated. A pending operation answers 202.

backup_operation_id.description: The verified backup taken before the update.

tools.title: Update stack identity metadata
tools.description: Update stack identity metadata

tools.title: Update stack identity if unchanged
tools.description: Revision-checked variant of the stack identity update. `If-Match` carries the `local_revision` read from the stack identity, in double quotes (for example `"3"`); a stale revision answers 412 and a reused `Idempotency-Key` with different content answers 409. The edit is stored locally and marked pending until it is synced with kombify Cloud. The body is limited to 4096 bytes. Requires the Postgres control plane (503 `stack_identity_store_unavailable` otherwise).

if_match.description: Strong local revision in double quotes, for example `"3"`.

tools.title: Update wallet item
tools.description: Merges the supplied fields into an item the caller owns and returns it redacted. Fields that are not supplied keep their value, including the stored secret and TOTP, which this contract can neither read nor change: the person sets those in the Wallet. The item kind and owner are immutable. An item owned by someone else answers 404. Only deployments that keep credentials in Techstack's own Wallet serve this route; elsewhere it answers 409 `self_hosted_only`.

notes.description: Free text; never put credentials here.

tools.title: Refresh the current node-owned connector through a distinct read-only job
tools.description: Retains the original signed setup operation and exact receipt, requires current published catalog and positive backend node/resource authority, and never reissues setup. Ordinary authenticated inventory reconciliation uses the same consumer for stale projections. Current v0.51.8 remains nondispatchable SourcePreview.

tools.title: Finish a service move
tools.description: Accepts a service copy that is pending verification as running and archives the migrating source copy. Answers 409 when the service is not pending verification. Today every call answers 501 until a runtime executor exists, and the canonical inventory store answers 503 `service_control_server_fence_unavailable`.
